question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward who has loose stools after a course of antibiotics is asked which action is the MOST appropriate.
option_1: Give him a hot meal with a lot of spice
option_2: Stop all fluids and give a strong pain killer
option_3: Collect a stool sample and care for his skin
option_4: Ask the family to take him home at once
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Collect a stool sample and care for his skin

Clinical Rationale: Loose stools after antibiotics point to a gut infection, so a stool sample is collected and the skin around him is cared for.

Key Clue: loose stools after a course of antibiotics

Priority Principle: Antibiotic associated diarrhoea

Why Not Others: (a) Spicy food may make the stools worse; (b) Stopping fluids may dry him out; (d) Taking him home delays his care.

PGI Exam Trap: All fluids are stopped and a pain killer is given.

5-Second Recall: Collect a stool sample and care for his skin.

PNC Exam Pearl: Antibiotics and loose stools mean send a sample.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward who is given a strong pain killer notes that his breathing has become slow and shallow. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Give the next dose early to settle him
option_2: Stop the drug and call the doctor at once
option_3: Ask him to walk to deepen his breathing
option_4: Note it and check again in an hour
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Stop the drug and call the doctor at once

Clinical Rationale: A strong pain killer can slow the breathing, so when it becomes slow and shallow the drug is stopped and the doctor called at once.

Key Clue: slow shallow breathing after a strong pain killer

Priority Principle: Opioid induced slow breathing

Why Not Others: (a) An early dose deepens the slow breathing; (c) Walking while drowsy is unsafe; (d) Waiting an hour risks his life.

PGI Exam Trap: The next dose is given early to settle him.

5-Second Recall: Stop the drug and call the doctor at once.

PNC Exam Pearl: Slow breath after a pain killer means stop.

question: A community nurse visiting a family is asked which statement about the management of a person with tuberculosis at home is the MOST appropriate.
option_1: The drugs are taken daily for the full course without a break
option_2: The drugs are taken for a week and then stopped
option_3: The drugs are shared with the family members
option_4: The drugs are taken for a month and then paused
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) The drugs are taken daily for the full course without a break

Clinical Rationale: Tuberculosis drugs must be taken daily for the full course without a break, so that the germs are killed and do NOT become resistant.

Key Clue: the management of tuberculosis at home

Priority Principle: Tuberculosis treatment

Why Not Others: (b) A week of drugs leaves the germs alive; (c) Drugs are not shared with others; (d) Pausing lets the germs grow back.

PGI Exam Trap: The drugs are shared with the family members.

5-Second Recall: The drugs are taken daily for the full course.

PNC Exam Pearl: Full course, every day, no break.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward is asked which statement about a sterile field is the MOST appropriate.
option_1: The field is kept near a busy doorway
option_2: The field stays sterile after it is left open
option_3: A dry field is touched with wet gloves
option_4: Anything below the level of the waist is treated as spoiled
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Anything below the level of the waist is treated as spoiled

Clinical Rationale: In a sterile field anything below the level of the waist is out of sight and is treated as spoiled, so it is NOT used.

Key Clue: the rules for a sterile field

Priority Principle: Sterile field

Why Not Others: (a) A busy doorway carries dust onto it; (b) An open field picks up germs from the air; (c) Wet gloves soak the field and spoil it.

PGI Exam Trap: The field is left open and is still called sterile.

5-Second Recall: Anything below the waist is treated as spoiled.

PNC Exam Pearl: Below the waist means out of play.

question: A nurse caring for a woman on the postnatal ward is asked which statement about a womb that stays soft after birth is the MOST appropriate.
option_1: It shows that the womb is very healthy
option_2: It points to a risk of heavy bleeding and is watched
option_3: It means that no bleeding will follow
option_4: It shows that the placenta is still inside
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) It points to a risk of heavy bleeding and is watched

Clinical Rationale: A womb that stays soft after birth does NOT squeeze the blood vessels, so it points to a risk of heavy bleeding and is watched closely.

Key Clue: a womb that stays soft after birth

Priority Principle: Atonic womb

Why Not Others: (a) A soft womb is a danger, not a healthy sign; (c) Heavy bleeding may follow a soft womb; (d) A soft womb does not show the placenta.

PGI Exam Trap: A soft womb after birth is called very healthy.

5-Second Recall: It points to a risk of heavy bleeding and is watched.

PNC Exam Pearl: Soft womb after birth means watch the bleeding.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward who has just returned from a thyroid operation notes a swelling at the neck and a change in his voice. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Ask him to lie flat and sleep
option_2: Give him a cold drink at once
option_3: Keep the airway free and call the doctor
option_4: Note it for the next ward round
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Keep the airway free and call the doctor

Clinical Rationale: A swelling at the neck with a changed voice after thyroid surgery points to bleeding that can block the airway, so the airway is kept free and the doctor called.

Key Clue: a neck swelling after thyroid surgery

Priority Principle: Airway risk after thyroid surgery

Why Not Others: (a) Lying flat may block the breathing; (b) A cold drink does not free the airway; (d) Waiting risks a blocked airway.

PGI Exam Trap: The swelling is noted for the next ward round.

5-Second Recall: Keep the airway free and call the doctor.

PNC Exam Pearl: Neck swelling after thyroid blocks the airway.

question: A nurse caring for a child on the ward who has diarrhoea and vomiting notes a sunken soft spot and no tears when the child cries. Which action is the MOST important for the nurse to take?
option_1: Wait and check the child in the morning
option_2: Hold back all fluids for a full day
option_3: Give plain water in very large amounts
option_4: Give oral rehydration fluid and tell the doctor
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Give oral rehydration fluid and tell the doctor

Clinical Rationale: A sunken soft spot with no tears points to NOT enough fluid, so oral rehydration fluid is given and the doctor told.

Key Clue: a sunken soft spot with no tears in a child

Priority Principle: Dehydration in a child

Why Not Others: (a) Waiting a night lets the child worsen; (b) Holding back fluids makes the loss worse; (c) Plain water alone does not replace salts.

PGI Exam Trap: All fluids are held back for a full day.

5-Second Recall: Give oral rehydration fluid and tell the doctor.

PNC Exam Pearl: Sunken spot, no tears means dried out.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward is asked which statement about a leg ulcer from poor arteries is the MOST appropriate.
option_1: The pain is worse when the leg is raised in bed
option_2: A firm bandage is put on the leg to heal it
option_3: The pain eases when he walks about the ward
option_4: The leg is kept up high so that it heals
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) The pain is worse when the leg is raised in bed

Clinical Rationale: An ulcer from poor arteries hurts more when the leg is raised, because the flow of blood to the foot falls still further.

Key Clue: the signs of a leg ulcer from poor arteries

Priority Principle: Arterial leg ulcer

Why Not Others: (b) A firm bandage is used for vein ulcers; (c) Walking often makes the pain worse; (d) Keeping the leg high worsens the flow.

PGI Exam Trap: A firm bandage is put on the leg to heal an arterial ulcer.

5-Second Recall: The pain is worse when the leg is raised in bed.

PNC Exam Pearl: Raise the leg, worse the pain.

question: A community nurse finds that a village has many cases of loose stools with quick drying of the body. Which action is the MOST important for the nurse to take FIRST?
option_1: Wait for the doctor to visit the next day
option_2: Start oral rehydration for the sick ones at once
option_3: Advise the families to stop all fluids
option_4: Give a strong pain killer to each person
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Start oral rehydration for the sick ones at once

Clinical Rationale: Many cases of loose stools with quick drying point to a spread of cholera, so oral rehydration is started at once to save the sick.

Key Clue: loose stools with quick drying in a village

Priority Principle: Cholera outbreak

Why Not Others: (a) Waiting a day risks many deaths; (c) Stopping fluids makes the drying worse; (d) A pain killer does not replace the lost fluid.

PGI Exam Trap: All fluids are stopped for the sick people.

5-Second Recall: Start oral rehydration for the sick ones at once.

PNC Exam Pearl: Watery stools mean fluids now.

question: A nurse caring for a child on the ward who has croup notes a harsh noise when the child breathes in and out. Which action is the MOST appropriate for the nurse to take?
option_1: Keep the child calm and give humidified oxygen
option_2: Ask the child to cry as loudly as possible
option_3: Give the child a large meal at once
option_4: Leave the child alone to sleep
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Keep the child calm and give humidified oxygen

Clinical Rationale: A harsh noise on breathing in and out in croup points to a narrow airway, so the child is kept calm and given humidified oxygen.

Key Clue: a harsh noise on breathing in croup

Priority Principle: Croup

Why Not Others: (b) Crying tightens the narrow airway; (c) A large meal may make the breathing worse; (d) Leaving the child alone misses the distress.

PGI Exam Trap: The child is asked to cry as loudly as possible.

5-Second Recall: Keep the child calm and give humidified oxygen.

PNC Exam Pearl: Calm the child, moist the air.

question: A nurse on the ward must set the order of steps to give a bed bath to a man. In which order should the nurse take the FIRST steps?
option_1: Wash the back FIRST, then the face, then the arms
option_2: Wash the trunk FIRST, then the face, then the legs
option_3: Wash the legs FIRST, then the face, then the arms
option_4: Wash the face FIRST, then the arms, then the trunk
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Wash the face FIRST, then the arms, then the trunk

Clinical Rationale: The bed bath starts at the face and works down to the arms and trunk, so that the cleanest part is washed with the cleanest water.

Key Clue: the steps for giving a bed bath

Priority Principle: Bed bath order

Why Not Others: (a) The face comes before the back; (b) The clean face is washed before the trunk; (c) The face is washed first of all.

PGI Exam Trap: The legs are washed before the face in this bath.

5-Second Recall: Wash the face first, then the arms, then the trunk.

PNC Exam Pearl: Face, arms, trunk.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward is asked which statement about the normal temperature of the body is the MOST appropriate.
option_1: It is about 30 degrees Celsius
option_2: It is about 42 degrees Celsius
option_3: It is about 37 degrees Celsius
option_4: It cannot be measured in a man
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) It is about 37 degrees Celsius

Clinical Rationale: The normal temperature of the body is about 37 degrees Celsius, which shows the heat is balanced within the body.

Key Clue: the normal body temperature

Priority Principle: Body temperature

Why Not Others: (a) About 30 degrees is far too low; (b) About 42 degrees is a high fever; (d) Temperature is measured in every client.

PGI Exam Trap: A temperature of about 42 degrees is called normal.

5-Second Recall: It is about 37 degrees Celsius.

PNC Exam Pearl: About 37 is the normal.

Reference Table: Normal adult vital signs - Temperature: 36.1-37.2 C (97-99 F); Pulse: 60-100 /min; Respiration: 12-20 /min; Blood pressure: < 120/80 mmHg; SpO2: 95-100% (COPD target 88-92%).

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward notes that his blood sodium is 128 mEq/L after days of vomiting. Which action is the MOST appropriate for the nurse to take?
option_1: Report it and watch for confusion and fits
option_2: Give him plain water in large amounts
option_3: Tell him that the level is quite normal
option_4: Ask him to walk fast to the bathroom
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Report it and watch for confusion and fits

Clinical Rationale: A blood sodium of 128 mEq/L is low after days of vomiting, so it is reported and he is watched for confusion and fits.

Key Clue: a blood sodium of 128 mEq/L after vomiting

Priority Principle: Hyponatraemia

Why Not Others: (b) Plain water in large amounts lowers it more; (c) The level is below the normal range; (d) Fast walking is unsafe with a low sodium.

PGI Exam Trap: The level is called normal and nothing is done.

5-Second Recall: Report it and watch for confusion and fits.

PNC Exam Pearl: 128 is low, watch the brain.

Reference Table: Normal serum electrolyte ranges - Sodium (Na+): 135-145 mEq/L; Potassium (K+): 3.5-5.0 mEq/L; Chloride (Cl-): 98-106 mEq/L; Calcium (total): 8.5-10.5 mg/dL; Magnesium (Mg2+): 1.5-2.5 mEq/L; Phosphate: 3.0-4.5 mg/dL.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward who has a chest injury notes that the wind pipe has shifted to one side and his neck veins are full. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Note it and wait for the ward round
option_2: Ask him to walk to test his breathing
option_3: Give him a large hot drink and wait
option_4: Call for help and give oxygen at once
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Call for help and give oxygen at once

Clinical Rationale: A shifted wind pipe with full neck veins after a chest injury points to air trapped in the chest, so help is called and oxygen given at once.

Key Clue: a shifted wind pipe with full neck veins after a chest injury

Priority Principle: Tension pneumothorax

Why Not Others: (a) Waiting risks a sudden collapse; (b) Walking uses more oxygen and strains him; (c) A hot drink does not free the trapped air.

PGI Exam Trap: The sign is noted and the ward round is awaited.

5-Second Recall: Call for help and give oxygen at once.

PNC Exam Pearl: Shifted wind pipe means call for help.

question: A nurse caring for a woman on the ward who takes digoxin is asked which finding is the MOST important to report.
option_1: A calm mood during the day
option_2: A good appetite with a steady pulse
option_3: A loss of appetite with a slow pulse and blurred vision
option_4: A steady pulse of 80 bpm with warm hands
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) A loss of appetite with a slow pulse and blurred vision

Clinical Rationale: A loss of appetite with a slow pulse and blurred vision on digoxin points to a level that has gone too high, so it is reported at once.

Key Clue: a loss of appetite with a slow pulse on digoxin

Priority Principle: Digoxin toxicity

Why Not Others: (a) A calm mood is not a drug warning; (b) A good appetite with a steady pulse is normal; (d) A steady pulse of 80 bpm is normal.

PGI Exam Trap: A good appetite is reported as too much digoxin.

5-Second Recall: A loss of appetite with a slow pulse is reported.

PNC Exam Pearl: Not hungry and slow pulse means the level is high.

Reference Table: Therapeutic drug levels & monitoring - Digoxin: 0.5-2.0 ng/mL (toxic > 2.0); Lithium: 0.6-1.2 mEq/L (toxic > 1.5); Phenytoin: 10-20 mcg/mL; INR (warfarin): Therapeutic 2-3; aPTT (heparin): 1.5-2.5 x control.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward who has a chest tube in place notes that the tube becomes disconnected from the drain. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Ask the man to take a deep breath
option_2: Clamp the tube and call for help at once
option_3: Leave the tube open and wait
option_4: Note it and change the drain later
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Clamp the tube and call for help at once

Clinical Rationale: If a chest tube comes off the drain, air can enter the chest, so the tube is clamped at once and help is called.

Key Clue: a chest tube disconnected from the drain

Priority Principle: Disconnected chest tube

Why Not Others: (a) A deep breath does not stop air from entering; (c) Leaving it open lets air enter the chest; (d) Waiting lets air trap in the chest.

PGI Exam Trap: The tube is left open while help is awaited.

5-Second Recall: Clamp the tube and call for help at once.

PNC Exam Pearl: Tube off the drain means clamp and call.

question: A nurse on the ward must set the order of steps to give a newborn its FIRST breast feed. In which order should the nurse take the FIRST steps?
option_1: Place it on the mother, help it to suckle, then dry it
option_2: Help it to suckle FIRST and then dry the baby
option_3: Dry the baby, place it on the mother, then help it to suckle
option_4: Wrap the baby warm and give it to the family
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Dry the baby, place it on the mother, then help it to suckle

Clinical Rationale: The newborn is dried, placed on the mother, and then helped to suckle, so that it stays warm and takes the FIRST milk.

Key Clue: the steps for the FIRST breast feed

Priority Principle: First feed order

Why Not Others: (a) Drying the baby comes first of all; (b) The baby is dried before it is put to the breast; (d) The first feed is given by the mother, not the family.

PGI Exam Trap: The baby is given to the family before the FIRST feed.

5-Second Recall: Dry the baby, place it on the mother, then help it to suckle.

PNC Exam Pearl: Dry, place, then feed.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward who has a head injury notes that he is becoming drowsy and his pulse is slowing. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Note it and wait for the ward round
option_2: Give him a drink and let him rest
option_3: Ask him to walk to test his balance
option_4: Check his airway and call for help
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Check his airway and call for help

Clinical Rationale: Drowsiness with a slowing pulse after a head injury points to rising pressure in the brain, so his airway is checked and help called at once.

Key Clue: drowsiness with a slowing pulse after a head injury

Priority Principle: Raised brain pressure

Why Not Others: (a) Waiting for the round risks his life; (b) A drink while drowsy risks choking; (c) Walking is unsafe with this sign.

PGI Exam Trap: The sign is noted and the ward round is awaited.

5-Second Recall: Check his airway and call for help.

PNC Exam Pearl: Drowsy and slow pulse mean call for help.

Reference Table: Normal adult vital signs - Temperature: 36.1-37.2 C (97-99 F); Pulse: 60-100 /min; Respiration: 12-20 /min; Blood pressure: < 120/80 mmHg; SpO2: 95-100% (COPD target 88-92%).

question: A community nurse visits a home where a man with a long term illness has a deep wound with a bad smell. Which action is the MOST appropriate for the nurse to take FIRST?
option_1: Assess the wound and clean it with the right dressing
option_2: Tell the family that the wound is quite normal
option_3: Leave the wound covered for a full month
option_4: Ask the family to stop all care at home
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Assess the wound and clean it with the right dressing

Clinical Rationale: A deep smelly wound needs proper care, so the nurse assesses it and cleans it with a dressing chosen for the wound.

Key Clue: a deep smelly wound at home

Priority Principle: Wound care at home

Why Not Others: (b) A smelly deep wound is not normal; (c) A month without care lets it worsen; (d) Stopping care leaves the wound untreated.

PGI Exam Trap: The wound is left covered for a full month.

5-Second Recall: Assess the wound and clean it with the right dressing.

PNC Exam Pearl: Smelly wound needs a proper dressing.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward is asked which statement about a shallow wound with a small amount of blood is the MOST appropriate.
option_1: It is left open to the air in a busy ward
option_2: It is cleaned with normal saline and covered with a dry dressing
option_3: It is rubbed with a strong spirit each hour
option_4: It is covered with a soiled cloth from the bed
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) It is cleaned with normal saline and covered with a dry dressing

Clinical Rationale: A shallow wound with a little blood is cleaned with normal saline and covered with a dry dressing, so that germs do NOT enter.

Key Clue: the care of a shallow wound

Priority Principle: Wound care

Why Not Others: (a) An open wound in a busy ward picks up germs; (c) A strong spirit each hour harms the skin; (d) A soiled cloth carries germs to the wound.

PGI Exam Trap: The wound is left open to the air in a busy ward.

5-Second Recall: It is cleaned with normal saline and covered with a dry dressing.

PNC Exam Pearl: Clean with saline, cover it dry.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward is shown a report with a blood glucose of 320 mg/dL and he is very thirsty and passing much urine. Which action is the MOST appropriate for the nurse to take?
option_1: Report it and give fluids and insulin as ordered
option_2: Give him a large sweet drink at once
option_3: Tell him that the level is quite normal
option_4: Hold all fluids to reduce the urine
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Report it and give fluids and insulin as ordered

Clinical Rationale: A blood glucose of 320 mg/dL with thirst and much urine points to high sugar, so it is reported and fluids with insulin are given as ordered.

Key Clue: a blood glucose of 320 mg/dL with much urine

Priority Principle: Hyperglycaemia

Why Not Others: (b) A sweet drink raises the sugar more; (c) The level is well above normal; (d) Holding fluids lets him dry out.

PGI Exam Trap: A large sweet drink is given at a glucose of 320 mg/dL.

5-Second Recall: Report it and give fluids and insulin as ordered.

PNC Exam Pearl: 320 is high, treat the sugar.

question: A nurse on the ward is asked which action is the MOST appropriate to stop the spread of germs from a man with a wound that is draining pus.
option_1: Wear gloves and touch other clients in between
option_2: Wear gloves and wash the hands after the dressing change
option_3: Use one dressing pack for two different clients
option_4: Leave the draining wound open to the air
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Wear gloves and wash the hands after the dressing change

Clinical Rationale: A draining wound carries germs, so gloves are worn and the hands are washed after the dressing change to stop the spread.

Key Clue: a wound that is draining pus

Priority Principle: Contact spread

Why Not Others: (a) Touching others with soiled gloves spreads the germs; (c) One pack for two clients spreads infection; (d) An open draining wound spreads the germs.

PGI Exam Trap: The draining wound is left open to the air of the ward.

5-Second Recall: Wear gloves and wash the hands after the dressing change.

PNC Exam Pearl: Gloves on, wash hands after.

question: A nurse caring for a woman in the labour room listens to the baby's heart and counts 100 beats per minute between pains. Which action is the MOST appropriate for the nurse to take?
option_1: Ask her to walk about the labour room
option_2: Tell her that the reading is quite normal
option_3: Report it and turn her on her left side
option_4: Note it and check again next hour
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Report it and turn her on her left side

Clinical Rationale: A baby's heart rate of 100 beats per minute is below the normal range, so it is reported and the woman turned on her left side to improve the flow.

Key Clue: a baby heart rate of 100 bpm between pains

Priority Principle: Low baby heart rate

Why Not Others: (a) Walking may lower the flow further; (b) The reading is below the normal range; (d) Waiting an hour risks the baby.

PGI Exam Trap: The reading of 100 bpm is called normal.

5-Second Recall: Report it and turn her on her left side.

PNC Exam Pearl: 100 bpm is low, turn her left.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward who had a stroke 2 days ago notes that he suddenly becomes drowsy and one pupil is larger than the other. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Note it and wait for the ward round
option_2: Give him a drink and let him rest
option_3: Ask him to walk to test his strength
option_4: Call for help and check his breathing
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Call for help and check his breathing

Clinical Rationale: Drowsiness with one pupil larger than the other after a stroke points to swelling in the brain, so help is called and his breathing checked at once.

Key Clue: one pupil larger than the other after a stroke

Priority Principle: Raised brain pressure

Why Not Others: (a) Waiting for the round misses the danger; (b) A drink while drowsy risks choking; (c) Walking is unsafe with this sign.

PGI Exam Trap: The sign is noted and the ward round is awaited.

5-Second Recall: Call for help and check his breathing.

PNC Exam Pearl: Big pupil after a stroke means call for help.

question: A nurse caring for a child on the ward who has a severe asthma attack notes that the wheeze has become quiet and the child is drowsy. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Ask the child to run to test the lungs
option_2: Call for help and give oxygen at once
option_3: Give a large cold drink and wait
option_4: Note it and check again in an hour
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Call for help and give oxygen at once

Clinical Rationale: A quiet wheeze with drowsiness in a severe asthma attack points to a very tight airway and falling oxygen, so help is called and oxygen given at once.

Key Clue: a quiet wheeze with drowsiness in an asthma attack

Priority Principle: Silent chest

Why Not Others: (a) Running tightens the airway further; (c) A cold drink does not open the airway; (d) Waiting an hour risks the child.

PGI Exam Trap: The child is asked to run to test the lungs.

5-Second Recall: Call for help and give oxygen at once.

PNC Exam Pearl: Quiet chest in asthma means call for help.

question: A nurse caring for a woman in the antenatal clinic is asked which statement about a normal pregnancy is the MOST appropriate.
option_1: The womb shrinks as the months pass
option_2: The womb stays the same size all through
option_3: The womb grows steadily through the months
option_4: The womb cannot be felt in pregnancy
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) The womb grows steadily through the months

Clinical Rationale: In a normal pregnancy the womb grows steadily through the months, which shows the baby is growing well.

Key Clue: the growth of the womb in pregnancy

Priority Principle: Womb growth

Why Not Others: (a) The womb does not shrink in pregnancy; (b) The womb grows, and does not stay the same; (d) The womb is felt as it rises in the belly.

PGI Exam Trap: The womb is said to stay the same size all through.

5-Second Recall: The womb grows steadily through the months.

PNC Exam Pearl: Womb grows month by month.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward who is choking on a piece of food notes that he cannot speak and holds his throat. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Note it and wait for the ward round
option_2: Give him a large drink of water
option_3: Ask him to lie down and rest
option_4: Give back blows and abdominal thrusts at once
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Give back blows and abdominal thrusts at once

Clinical Rationale: A man who cannot speak and holds his throat while eating points to a blocked airway, so back blows and abdominal thrusts are given at once.

Key Clue: a man who cannot speak and holds his throat

Priority Principle: Choking

Why Not Others: (a) Waiting risks the man's life; (b) A drink may block the airway further; (c) Lying down does not clear the block.

PGI Exam Trap: The man is given a large drink of water for the block.

5-Second Recall: Give back blows and abdominal thrusts at once.

PNC Exam Pearl: Cannot speak means clear the airway.

question: A nurse caring for a woman on the ward is asked which action is the MOST appropriate during her panic attack.
option_1: Stay with her and speak in a calm, quiet voice
option_2: Tell her to breathe fast into a paper bag
option_3: Leave her alone until the attack passes
option_4: Hold her arms to keep her very still
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Stay with her and speak in a calm, quiet voice

Clinical Rationale: Staying with the woman and speaking calmly helps her feel safe and brings the panic down.

Key Clue: the care of a woman during a panic attack

Priority Principle: Panic attack

Why Not Others: (b) Fast breathing into a bag is not advised; (c) Leaving her alone adds to the fear; (d) Holding her arms adds to the panic.

PGI Exam Trap: The woman is left alone until the attack passes.

5-Second Recall: Stay with her and speak in a calm voice.

PNC Exam Pearl: Stay calm and stay near.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward who is started on a new antibiotic by drip develops a swollen face and a tight chest. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Give him a warm drink of milk
option_2: Slow the drip and watch him
option_3: Stop the drip and call the doctor
option_4: Finish the dose and then report
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Stop the drip and call the doctor

Clinical Rationale: A swollen face with a tight chest during a new antibiotic drip points to a severe allergy, so the drip is stopped and the doctor called at once.

Key Clue: a swollen face with a tight chest during a drip

Priority Principle: Anaphylaxis

Why Not Others: (a) A warm drink does not treat this; (b) Slowing the drip still feeds the allergy; (d) Finishing the dose is dangerous here.

PGI Exam Trap: The dose is finished and then reported.

5-Second Recall: Stop the drip and call the doctor.

PNC Exam Pearl: Swollen face on a drip means stop it.

question: A community nurse visiting a family is shown a growth chart where a child's weight is below the third line for age. Which action is the MOST important for the nurse to take?
option_1: Tell the family that the weight is quite normal
option_2: Assess the diet and begin feeding support
option_3: Ask the family to give only sweet drinks
option_4: Note it and review the child next year
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Assess the diet and begin feeding support

Clinical Rationale: A weight below the third line for age points to poor growth, so the diet is assessed and feeding support is begun.

Key Clue: a growth chart with weight below the third line for age

Priority Principle: Poor growth

Why Not Others: (a) The weight is below the normal lines; (c) Sweet drinks do not build weight or health; (d) A year later is far too late.

PGI Exam Trap: The family is asked to give only sweet drinks.

5-Second Recall: Assess the diet and begin feeding support.

PNC Exam Pearl: Below the third line means feed the child.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward who has a chest tube removed notes that he becomes breathless with air leaking from the wound. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Press a sterile dressing on the site and call for help
option_2: Ask him to take a deep breath and lie flat
option_3: Leave the site and note it for the round
option_4: Give him a hot drink and let him rest
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Press a sterile dressing on the site and call for help

Clinical Rationale: Breathlessness with air leaking from the wound after a chest tube is out points to air entering the chest, so a sterile dressing is pressed on and help called.

Key Clue: a small crackle of air at the wound after a chest tube

Priority Principle: Air leak

Why Not Others: (b) Lying flat may worsen his breathing; (c) Leaving the site lets air enter the chest; (d) A hot drink does not stop the air leak.

PGI Exam Trap: The site is left alone and noted for the round.

5-Second Recall: Press a sterile dressing on the site and call for help.

PNC Exam Pearl: Air at the wound means press and call.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward who is very ill hears the family ask to hide the diagnosis from him. Which action is the MOST appropriate for the nurse to take?
option_1: Tell other patients about his illness
option_2: Tell the family that his right is of no use
option_3: Hide the reports from the man himself
option_4: Ask the man how much he wishes to know
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Ask the man how much he wishes to know

Clinical Rationale: The man has a right to know about his own illness, so the nurse asks him how much he wishes to know before any step is taken.

Key Clue: a family asking to hide the diagnosis

Priority Principle: Right to information

Why Not Others: (a) Telling others is a breach of privacy; (b) His right to know is real and is respected; (c) Hiding reports goes against his right.

PGI Exam Trap: The reports are hidden from the man himself.

5-Second Recall: Ask the man how much he wishes to know.

PNC Exam Pearl: Ask the man what he wants to know.

question: A nurse caring for a woman on the postnatal ward notes that her legs are swollen and painful 3 days after delivery. Which action is the MOST appropriate for the nurse to take?
option_1: Keep the leg still and tell the doctor at once
option_2: Massage the leg to ease the pain
option_3: Ask her to walk around the ward
option_4: Put a warm pack on and then wait
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Keep the leg still and tell the doctor at once

Clinical Rationale: A swollen painful leg 3 days after delivery points to a deep vein clot, so the leg is kept still and the doctor told at once.

Key Clue: a swollen painful leg after delivery

Priority Principle: Deep vein thrombosis

Why Not Others: (b) Massage may break off the clot; (c) Walking may move the clot to the lung; (d) A warm pack does not treat the danger.

PGI Exam Trap: The leg is massaged to ease the pain.

5-Second Recall: Keep the leg still and tell the doctor at once.

PNC Exam Pearl: Swollen leg after birth means a clot.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward who is very quiet and has stopped eating for a week is asked which action is the MOST important FIRST.
option_1: Leave him alone and let him eat when ready
option_2: Sit with him at meals and watch his intake
option_3: Give him a large meal and walk away
option_4: Tell him that he must eat every plate
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Sit with him at meals and watch his intake

Clinical Rationale: A man who has stopped eating for a week is at risk, so the nurse sits with him at meals and watches his intake closely.

Key Clue: a man who has stopped eating for a week

Priority Principle: Poor intake in low mood

Why Not Others: (a) Leaving him alone lets the poor intake go on; (c) A large meal left with him is wasted; (d) A strict order adds to his distress.

PGI Exam Trap: He is left alone to eat when ready.

5-Second Recall: Sit with him at meals and watch his intake.

PNC Exam Pearl: Sit with him, watch the plate.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward is asked which statement about a nasogastric tube left in place is the MOST appropriate.
option_1: The feed is given fast while the man lies flat
option_2: The tube is left without any check at all
option_3: The position of the tube is checked before every feed
option_4: The tube is pulled out by the man himself
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) The position of the tube is checked before every feed

Clinical Rationale: The position of a nasogastric tube is checked before every feed, so that the feed does NOT go into the airway.

Key Clue: the care of a nasogastric tube in place

Priority Principle: Nasogastric tube

Why Not Others: (a) A fast feed with the man flat may choke him; (b) The tube is checked before each feed; (d) The tube is not pulled out by the man.

PGI Exam Trap: The tube is left in place with no check before the feed.

5-Second Recall: The position of the tube is checked before every feed.

PNC Exam Pearl: Check the tube, then feed.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward who is given a water tablet each morning notes that he is dizzy on standing. Which action is the MOST appropriate for the nurse to take?

option_2: Give the tablet twice a day at once
option_3: Ask him to stand up very quickly
option_4: Check his blood pressure and tell the doctor
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Check his blood pressure and tell the doctor

Clinical Rationale: A water tablet can lower the blood pressure and cause dizziness on standing, so his pressure is checked and the doctor told.

Key Clue: dizziness on standing while taking a water tablet

Priority Principle: Postural fall in pressure

Why Not Others: (a) Stopping fluids does not treat this; (b) A double dose may drop the pressure further; (c) Standing quickly adds to the dizziness.

PGI Exam Trap: The tablet is given twice a day to stop the dizziness.

5-Second Recall: Check his blood pressure and tell the doctor.

PNC Exam Pearl: Dizzy on standing means check the pressure.

Reference Table: Normal adult vital signs - Temperature: 36.1-37.2 C (97-99 F); Pulse: 60-100 /min; Respiration: 12-20 /min; Blood pressure: < 120/80 mmHg; SpO2: 95-100% (COPD target 88-92%).

question: A nurse caring for a woman on the ward who is very sad is asked which action is the MOST important to keep her safe FIRST.
option_1: Tell her that she has much to live for
option_2: Ask her plainly about any thoughts of harming herself
option_3: Leave her alone until she asks for help
option_4: Give her a job to keep her busy
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Ask her plainly about any thoughts of harming herself

Clinical Rationale: A very sad woman may think of harming herself, so she is asked plainly about her safety so that the risk is known and met.

Key Clue: a very sad woman on the ward

Priority Principle: Risk of self harm

Why Not Others: (a) Saying she has much to live for does not lower the risk; (c) Leaving her alone misses the danger; (d) A busy job does not answer the risk.

PGI Exam Trap: She is left alone until she asks for help.

5-Second Recall: Ask her plainly about any thoughts of harming herself.

PNC Exam Pearl: Low mood means ask about safety.

question: A nurse on the ward is asked which statement about cleaning the hands with an alcohol rub is the MOST appropriate.
option_1: It is used when the hands are NOT visibly dirty
option_2: It is used when the hands are covered in dirt
option_3: It takes the place of washing the hands with soap
option_4: It is used once at the end of the day
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) It is used when the hands are NOT visibly dirty

Clinical Rationale: An alcohol rub kills germs when the hands are NOT visibly dirty, while dirty hands are washed with soap and water.

Key Clue: the use of an alcohol hand rub

Priority Principle: Hand hygiene

Why Not Others: (b) Dirty hands need soap and water first; (c) It does not replace soap when hands are soiled; (d) The hands are cleaned many times a day.

PGI Exam Trap: An alcohol rub is used when the hands are covered in dirt.

5-Second Recall: It is used when the hands are not visibly dirty.

PNC Exam Pearl: Clean hands, rub is fine.

question: A nurse caring for a woman in the antenatal clinic is asked which statement about the danger signs in pregnancy is the MOST appropriate.
option_1: Blurring of vision is the usual in pregnancy
option_2: Bleeding from the vagina is the usual in pregnancy

option_4: Bleeding from the vagina is a danger sign to report at once
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Bleeding from the vagina is a danger sign to report at once

Clinical Rationale: Bleeding from the vagina in pregnancy is a danger sign and is reported at once, as it may point to a serious problem.

Key Clue: the danger signs in pregnancy

Priority Principle: Danger signs

Why Not Others: (a) Blurring of vision needs urgent care; (b) Bleeding in pregnancy is not the usual; (c) A severe headache points to a problem.

PGI Exam Trap: Bleeding from the vagina is called the usual in pregnancy.

5-Second Recall: Bleeding from the vagina is a danger sign to report.

PNC Exam Pearl: Bleeding in pregnancy means report now.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward who is on a course of an antibiotic for many days develops a sore mouth with white patches. Which action is the MOST appropriate for the nurse to take?
option_1: Stop all fluids and all food
option_2: Give a stronger antibiotic at once
option_3: Report it and give mouth care as ordered
option_4: Ignore it as it will settle on its own
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Report it and give mouth care as ordered

Clinical Rationale: A sore mouth with white patches on long antibiotics points to a fungal infection, so it is reported and mouth care is given as ordered.

Key Clue: a sore mouth with white patches on antibiotics

Priority Principle: Oral thrush

Why Not Others: (a) Stopping fluids and food weakens him; (b) A stronger antibiotic does not treat a fungus; (d) Ignoring it lets the infection spread.

PGI Exam Trap: A stronger antibiotic is given at once for the white patches.

PNC Exam Pearl: White patches on antibiotics mean thrush.

question: A nurse on the ward is shown an ampoule of a strong drug with the dose written as 1 mg in 1 mL. The order reads 0.5 mg. Which amount should the nurse draw?
option_1: 1 mL
option_2: 0.5 mL
option_3: 2 mL
option_4: 5 mL
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) 0.5 mL

Why Not Others: (a) 1 mL would give a double dose; (c) 2 mL would give a far larger dose; (d) 5 mL would give a very large dose.

5-Second Recall: Draw 0.5 mL for an order of 0.5 mg.

PNC Exam Pearl: Half the dose means half the volume.

question: A nurse manager on the ward is shown a record where the drug given was written an hour after it was due. Which action is the MOST appropriate for the manager to take FIRST?
option_1: Ask the nurse for the reason and note it in the record
option_2: Rub out the time and write a fresh one

option_4: Punish the nurse in front of the others
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Ask the nurse for the reason and note it in the record

Clinical Rationale: A late drug entry is asked about and noted truly in the record, so the reason is known and the care can be made safer.

Key Clue: a drug entry written an hour after it was due

Priority Principle: Late drug entry

Why Not Others: (b) Rubbing out the time hides the truth; (c) Ignoring it makes the same error happen again; (d) Public punishment breaks the team.

PGI Exam Trap: The wrong time is rubbed out and a fresh one written.

5-Second Recall: Ask the nurse for the reason and note it in the record.

PNC Exam Pearl: Ask the reason, note it true.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward who has heart failure notes that his ankles are swollen and he gains 2 kg in a week. Which finding is the MOST important for the nurse to report?
option_1: A calm mood through the whole day
option_2: A steady pulse of 78 bpm with warm hands

option_4: Increasing breathlessness with a rising weight
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Increasing breathlessness with a rising weight

Clinical Rationale: Swollen ankles with a fast weight gain point to fluid building up, so increasing breathlessness is reported at once as the heart fails further.

Key Clue: a weight gain of 2 kg in a week with heart failure

Priority Principle: Fluid overload

Why Not Others: (a) A calm mood is not a warning sign; (b) A steady pulse of 78 bpm is normal; (c) A good appetite does not show fluid.

PGI Exam Trap: The steady pulse is reported as the danger sign.

5-Second Recall: Increasing breathlessness with a rising weight is reported.

PNC Exam Pearl: Fast weight gain means fluid in the body.

Reference Table: Normal adult vital signs - Temperature: 36.1-37.2 C (97-99 F); Pulse: 60-100 /min; Respiration: 12-20 /min; Blood pressure: < 120/80 mmHg; SpO2: 95-100% (COPD target 88-92%).

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward is asked which statement about the storage of insulin is the MOST appropriate.
option_1: It is shaken hard before it is drawn
option_2: It is kept in the freezer to stay fresh
option_3: It is kept in a cool dark place and NOT frozen
option_4: It is used after the date has passed
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) It is kept in a cool dark place and NOT frozen

Clinical Rationale: Insulin is kept cool and in the dark and never frozen, so that the drug stays active and safe to give.

Key Clue: the correct storage of insulin

Why Not Others: (a) Shaking hard spoils the insulin; (b) Freezing destroys the insulin; (d) An old date may mean spoilt insulin.

PGI Exam Trap: Insulin is kept in the freezer and called fresh.

5-Second Recall: It is kept in a cool dark place and not frozen.

PNC Exam Pearl: Cool, dark, never frozen.

question: A nurse manager on the ward is asked which statement about a written record of care is the MOST appropriate.
option_1: It is written in pencil and rubbed out later
option_2: It is written from memory at the end of the week
option_3: It is left blank for the next nurse to fill
option_4: It is written at the time of care and signed by the nurse
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) It is written at the time of care and signed by the nurse

Clinical Rationale: A record of care is written at the time it is given and signed by the nurse, so that the care can be trusted as true.

Key Clue: the writing of a care record

Priority Principle: Care record

Why Not Others: (a) Pencil records can be changed and are unsafe; (b) Writing from memory makes it untrue; (c) Blank records hide the care that was given.

PGI Exam Trap: The record is written from memory at the end of the week.

5-Second Recall: It is written at the time of care and signed by the nurse.

PNC Exam Pearl: Write it then, sign it there.

question: A community nurse finds that 60 percent of the children in a village are NOT fully immunised. Which action is the MOST appropriate for the nurse to take?
option_1: Wait for the families to come to the clinic

option_4: Set the records aside and take no action
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Plan a vaccination camp in the village

Key Clue: 60 percent of children NOT fully immunised

Priority Principle: Low immunisation coverage

Why Not Others: (a) Waiting for them to come delays the work; (b) Blaming the families does not raise coverage; (d) Setting the records aside ignores the gap.

PGI Exam Trap: The records are set aside with no action taken.

5-Second Recall: Plan a vaccination camp in the village.

PNC Exam Pearl: Missed doses mean go to the village.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward is asked which statement about a normal urine output is the MOST appropriate.
option_1: It is about ten litres in a day
option_2: It is about one and a half litres in a day
option_3: It is the same colour as dark tea
option_4: It stops completely after an operation
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) It is about one and a half litres in a day

Clinical Rationale: A normal adult passes about one and a half litres of urine in a day, which shows the kidneys are working well.

Key Clue: the normal daily urine output

Priority Principle: Urine output

Why Not Others: (a) Ten litres a day is far too much; (c) Dark tea colour suggests concentrated urine; (d) No urine after an operation must be reported.

PGI Exam Trap: Ten litres a day is called a normal output.

5-Second Recall: About one and a half litres in a day is normal.

PNC Exam Pearl: One and a half litres, clear and pale.

question: A nurse caring for a woman on the ward who takes digoxin notes a pulse of 48 bpm before the dose. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Hold the dose and tell the doctor
option_2: Give the dose as ordered at once
option_3: Give a double dose to catch up
option_4: Give a warm drink and then the dose
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Hold the dose and tell the doctor

Clinical Rationale: Digoxin slows the heart, so a pulse of 48 bpm before the dose means the drug is held and the doctor told at once.

Key Clue: a pulse of 48 bpm before a dose of digoxin

Priority Principle: Digoxin safety

Why Not Others: (b) Giving it at a pulse of 48 is unsafe; (c) A double dose is dangerous here; (d) A warm drink does not change the risk.

PGI Exam Trap: The dose is given even at a pulse of 48 bpm.

5-Second Recall: Hold the dose and tell the doctor.

PNC Exam Pearl: Slow pulse, hold the digoxin.

question: A community nurse visiting a family is asked which statement about the cold chain for vaccines is the MOST appropriate.
option_1: The vaccines need no care in the summer heat

option_3: The vaccines are frozen and thawed many times
option_4: The vaccines are kept cool from the place of making to the child
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) The vaccines are kept cool from the place of making to the child

Key Clue: the cold chain for vaccines

Priority Principle: Cold chain

Why Not Others: (a) Vaccines need careful care in the heat; (b) Warmth spoils the vaccines; (c) Repeated freezing and thawing spoils them.

PGI Exam Trap: The vaccines are kept warm before they are used.

5-Second Recall: Vaccines stay cool from the making to the child.

PNC Exam Pearl: Keep them cool all the way.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward notes that his blood potassium is 6.5 mmol/L. Which action is the MOST important for the nurse to take?
option_1: Stop any potassium and tell the doctor at once
option_2: Give him a drink rich in potassium
option_3: Wait and recheck the level next week
option_4: Ask him to eat more bananas and dates
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Stop any potassium and tell the doctor at once

Clinical Rationale: A blood potassium of 6.5 mmol/L is dangerously high and can stop the heart, so potassium is stopped and the doctor told.

Key Clue: a blood potassium of 6.5 mmol/L

Priority Principle: Hyperkalaemia

Why Not Others: (b) A potassium drink would raise it further; (c) Waiting a week risks the heart; (d) Bananas and dates add more potassium.

PGI Exam Trap: A drink rich in potassium is given at this level.

5-Second Recall: Stop any potassium and tell the doctor at once.

PNC Exam Pearl: 6.5 is high, hold the potassium.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward who has a crush injury to the leg notes that his urine is dark and his pulse is rising. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Hold his fluids to rest the kidneys
option_2: Report it and give fluids as ordered
option_3: Ask him to walk to test the leg
option_4: Note it and wait for the ward round
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Report it and give fluids as ordered

Clinical Rationale: Dark urine with a rising pulse after a crush injury points to muscle breakdown harming the kidneys, so it is reported and fluids are given.

Key Clue: dark urine with a rising pulse after a crush injury

Priority Principle: Rhabdomyolysis

Why Not Others: (a) Holding fluids lets the kidneys be harmed more; (c) Walking strains the injured leg; (d) Waiting for the round risks the kidneys.

PGI Exam Trap: Fluids are held back to rest the kidneys.

5-Second Recall: Report it and give fluids as ordered.

PNC Exam Pearl: Dark urine after a crush means give fluids.

Reference Table: Normal adult vital signs - Temperature: 36.1-37.2 C (97-99 F); Pulse: 60-100 /min; Respiration: 12-20 /min; Blood pressure: < 120/80 mmHg; SpO2: 95-100% (COPD target 88-92%).

question: A nurse caring for a woman on the ward who has severe diarrhoea for 2 days notes that she feels weak and dizzy on standing. Which level is the MOST likely for the nurse to expect?
option_1: A high blood calcium level
option_2: A high blood potassium level

option_4: A high blood sugar level
solution:

Why Not Others: (a) Calcium is not the level lost here; (b) Diarrhoea lowers, not raises, potassium; (d) Blood sugar is not the level lost here.

PGI Exam Trap: A high blood potassium level is expected with diarrhoea.

5-Second Recall: A low blood potassium level is expected.

PNC Exam Pearl: Diarrhoea drains the salts.

Reference Table: Normal serum electrolyte ranges - Sodium (Na+): 135-145 mEq/L; Potassium (K+): 3.5-5.0 mEq/L; Chloride (Cl-): 98-106 mEq/L; Calcium (total): 8.5-10.5 mg/dL; Magnesium (Mg2+): 1.5-2.5 mEq/L; Phosphate: 3.0-4.5 mg/dL.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward who has an ileostomy notes a high output of watery stool and a dry mouth. Which finding is the MOST important for the nurse to watch?
option_1: A rising pulse with a falling urine output

solution:

Priority Principle: Fluid loss

Why Not Others: (b) A steady weight does not show the loss; (c) A good appetite is not a warning sign; (d) A calm mood does not show fluid loss.

PGI Exam Trap: A steady weight is watched as the danger sign.

5-Second Recall: A rising pulse with a falling urine output is watched.

PNC Exam Pearl: Fast pulse, less urine, more fluid lost.

Reference Table: Normal adult vital signs - Temperature: 36.1-37.2 C (97-99 F); Pulse: 60-100 /min; Respiration: 12-20 /min; Blood pressure: < 120/80 mmHg; SpO2: 95-100% (COPD target 88-92%).

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward who takes warfarin is asked which finding is the MOST important to report.
option_1: A good appetite at all meals
option_2: Bleeding gums with dark stools
option_3: A calm mood during the day
option_4: A steady pulse of 80 bpm

Correct Answer: (b) Bleeding gums with dark stools

Priority Principle: Warfarin overdose

Why Not Others: (a) A good appetite is reassuring; (c) A calm mood is not a bleeding sign; (d) A steady pulse of 80 bpm is normal.

PGI Exam Trap: A steady pulse of 80 bpm is reported as bleeding.

5-Second Recall: Bleeding gums with dark stools are reported.

PNC Exam Pearl: Gums bleed, warfarin is too much.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward who suddenly becomes very angry and clenches his fists is asked which action is the MOST appropriate FIRST.

option_3: Stay calm and keep a safe distance from him
option_4: Hold his arms to make him sit down

Why Not Others: (a) Turning her back puts the nurse at risk; (b) Standing close and ordering raises the anger; (d) Holding his arms may bring on a fight.

PGI Exam Trap: The nurse stands close and orders him to stop.

5-Second Recall: Stay calm and keep a safe distance from him.

PNC Exam Pearl: Anger means stay calm and keep space.

question: A community nurse on a home visit must set the order of steps for a safe delivery of care. In which order should the nurse take the FIRST steps?

option_3: Ask consent, examine the person, then introduce yourself
